result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): A puts booking a first session front and centre: real wheel/kiln slots with availability, reassuring copy (no experience needed, can change up to 4 hours before) and a 'Getting started' checklist that shows what happens after booking. B is clean and focused with good pottery wording and a short glossary, but it only shows step 1 of a choice. It gives no preview of slots or of what comes after, so the first action feels less concrete. A's credits sidebar adds a bit of secondary content, but it stays visually below the main booking panel. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): B makes booking the first session the obvious focus. It shows real open wheel slots with times and availability, and its 'Getting started' panel tells a new member what happens after they book, which makes the first action feel low-risk. A is clean and well focused, but it stops at an abstract 'wheel time or kiln slot' choice with no time slots, no clear button and no preview of what comes next, which leaves much of the screen empty. B is denser and adds a studio-credits panel the member doesn't need yet, but its wording is much more specific to a pottery studio.
